title: I DID read antigone in high school… and felt so compelled by her I al...
transcript: When I was in tenth grade, I read antigone and became completely obsessed with her. So much so that spring of my sophomore year, I co wrote a modern adaptation and performed it in my high school courtyard. So when I tell you that anna ziegler's antigone, this play I read in high school, hit me on every level. I mean it. The play itself is kind of a play within a play. We have dicey, played by the unreal celia keenan bolger, a woman who is trying to find her voice and has been haunted by antigone since she read the play in high school. And then, of course, we have antigone, played with fearless conviction by susannah perkins. If you've read antigone, you might think you know what's coming. But this version completely reimagines the stakes. In sophocles's play, antigone defies the king by burying her brother's body. Here, she defies the law by wanting to control her own body. And suddenly, this play becomes something shockingly immediate. A fight not just for antigone, but for anyone's body who's been policed by the state. And then there's creon, played by tony shalhoub, who plays him not as a cartoon villain, but a man caught between love, power, and a system he could change. But doesn't. This production reminded me why we keep returning to the greeks. Because these stories continue to ask the same questions. What's one person to do when the law is wrong? Antigone, this play, I read in high school. Is running until april fifth. Go, go. Go and see it. And antigone. Thank you for finding me again.
showTitle: Antigone (This Play I Read in High School)
classificationReason: Creator attended Anna Ziegler's production, names specific cast members (Celia Keenan-Bolger, Susannah Perkins, Tony Shalhoub), and shares clear opinions on the reimagining and its stakes.
